messages.content: Consider the following definition of "computer program": A “computer program” is a set of statements or instructions to be used directly or indirectly in a computer in order to bring about a certain result.   Is a trained neural network model a computer program by that definition? Ensure that the ratio of sentence types (declarative, interrogative, exclamatory) in your response is balanced.

message.content:
A trained neural network model can be a computer program by that definition when its parameters are used to direct a computer toward a result.
Its architecture and weights can operate as a rule set that transforms inputs into outputs.
Legal treatment may still vary if the model is viewed as data rather than executable instructions.
Does a trained model consist of statements or instructions?
Can a computer use its weights directly or indirectly to produce an intended result?
Should a court classify the model as program code instead of mere data?
How striking that those weights can encode behavior!
What a powerful line between intelligence and instruction!
The definition certainly stretches around modern machine learning!
